body:
Ava Ramos: :rotating_light: Flagging a regression after the traffic-routing rollout at 09:12PT. We're seeing a spike in quota DENY responses for customers that should be on the 'enterprise-exempt' list. Customer reports and internal 5xx/4xx alerts increasing.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-23911122 - routing rollout -> quota misclassification (severity: P1) — paging on-call.

Miguel Chen: I'm on pager, pulling logs now. Looking at request traces to see where exemptions are dropped. Seen same pattern in two clusters (us-west-2, eu-west-1).

Miguel Chen: quick grep on auth log shows header x-customer-tier present but our routing lambda isn't mapping it for 4% of requests: `mapping_key=null` — looks like a schema mismatch after the new router changed expected JSON path.

Samir Patel: I see the same in the canary logs. New routing module expects `customer.attributes.tier` but legacy tokens set `customer.tier`. The migration code has a fallback, but it's not firing for XX-tenant ids due to a null pointer check.

Priya Singh: Can we flip the feature flag to stop new router from being used for requests where mapping_key is null? We should kill the rollout to stop customer impact.

Ava Ramos: Yes, flip the kill-switch. Priority: stop user-facing errors.

deploy-bot: Received command: `/feature-flag disable routing.new_migration --scope=global --reason="quota misclassification causing DENY"` — starting rollout revert.

Miguel Chen: Executed kill-switch command. Verifying traffic now.

Priya Singh: Running quick check: `SELECT count(*) FROM request_logs WHERE routing_version='new' AND exemption_applied=false GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20;` — top tenants look like they have missing exemptions.

Samir Patel: Suggestion: apply a hotpatch that adds a compatibility shim reading both `customer.attributes.tier` and `customer.tier` before full rollback. That would avoid full traffic flip if safe.

Ava Ramos: For speed, prefer full rollback to stable router for now. We can patch after rollback.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: `orchestrator release rollback routing-service v2026.03.11 -> v2026.03.10` — rolling back 3 canary instances, then global.

incident-bot: Rollback in progress — will post progress updates. ETA ~6 minutes for global stabilization.

Miguel Chen: Doubling down on telemetry: enabling detailed sampling for denied requests to gather tenant ids and full request payloads: `telemetry.sample(rate=1, filter=quota:deny)`.

Priya Singh: Noted. I'm drafting customers/ops status update. Which customers are affected? Any enterprise SLAs impacted?

Samir Patel: Early counts: ~28 tenants hit with >50 denied requests/min in the last 10m. Two customers (ACME Corp, NovaPay) reported production errors. Both enterprise — will escalate to success managers.

Ava Ramos: Copy — escalate to CS and AM now. Priya, please coordinate status page and CS note. Miguel, keep collecting traces.

PagerDuty: @Miguel Chen acknowledged the page.

Miguel Chen: Rollback reached 60% global, error rate dropping in us-west-2. Still seeing a tail in eu-west-1. Patching health checks for that region.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete: routing-service is now v2026.03.10 globally. Canary metrics: error rate back to baseline in 90% of clusters.

Priya Singh: Posted status update to customers: "We've rolled back a routing change that caused some customers to receive quota errors. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with affected customers." Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/23911122

Ava Ramos: Good. Requesting a short mitigation report in-thread: who did what and next steps for postmortem.

Miguel Chen: Timeline (short):
- 09:12PT: routing.new_migration enabled to canary
- 09:23PT: internal alerts for quota DENY spike
- 09:25PT: page routed to on-call Miguel
- 09:35PT: kill-switch flipped, rollback started
- 09:42PT: rollback complete in most regions
- 09:55PT: full stabilization and status update posted

Samir Patel: Root cause hypothesis: routing migration changed JSON path for tier. Fallback logic had a null-check bug that caused exemptions lookup to skip for certain tenant payload shapes. Secondary issue: deployment didn't include integration test for legacy token shapes.

Priya Singh: Customer impact: two enterprise accounts with intermittent failed requests (ACME Corp ~13k requests affected, NovaPay ~4.2k). No billing anomalies observed yet but token accounting team should double-check spikes.

Ava Ramos: Action items:
- Samir: prepare hotfix patch to add compatibility shim and unit tests (owner: Samir, ETA 4h)
- Miguel: run a tenant-scan to list all tenants with legacy token shapes and produce a migration map (owner: Miguel, ETA 8h)
- Priya: coordinate CS outreach and postmortem writeup (owner: Priya, ETA 24h)
- Platform: add integration tests to CI for mixed token shapes in canary rollout pipeline (owner: eng-platform, ETA 72h)

deploy-bot: Adding incident tag: `regression:deploy-routing` and `impact:customer-facing`.

Ava Ramos: Any lessons about canary gating? We need stricter contract checks before flipping global.

Samir Patel: Agreed — propose a preflight that validates expected JSON paths across a sample of real traffic for 1hr before increasing canary percentage.

Priya Singh: I'll schedule a hotwash and invite CS, oncall, platform, and product tomorrow. Will create the postmortem doc and link here.

Miguel Chen: For the record: no increase in billing charges seen during the incident window, token-accounting team confirmed (message from @billing-bot: logs scanned). Will run deeper audit overnight.

Ava Ramos: Thanks everyone — I will stay on to triage followups. Keep updates short; put final postmortem link in this thread when ready.

Priya Singh: Postmortem created: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INC/23911122 — will update with timelines and RCA.

Ava Ramos: Closing incident channel once postmortem and customer notes are out. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident INC-23911122 resolved and closed by Ava Ramos\"
